reader_question: Our HTTP service can take up to two minutes to start. After startup, it sometimes temporarily cannot serve requests but recovers by itself; a deadlock instead needs a restart. How should startup, readiness and liveness probes divide these jobs, and what would be a reasonable initial startup budget?
reader_context: Kubernetes v1.34 Deployment, restartPolicy Always. Traffic uses a normal Kubernetes Service. The application team can implement appropriate HTTP health endpoints; no particular path or existing probe implementation is assumed.

mandatory.claim: Startup success enables readiness and liveness; repeated startup failure triggers a restart under Always.
Readiness failure stops normal Service traffic while the container keeps running; recovery allows it to become ready again.
Liveness should detect the unrecoverable deadlock; consecutive failures reaching its threshold trigger a container restart.
failureThreshold: 30 with periodSeconds: 5 gives an approximately 150-second startup allowance, exceeding the stated 120-second startup.
After startup, readiness and liveness are independent; readiness failure does not suspend liveness.

mandatory_qualifications: The timing is an initial configuration example, not an exact deadline or measurement of this application.
Health endpoints must implement these meanings; probe names do not diagnose application state by themselves.
Readiness governs Service traffic; do not claim it prevents every direct connection.

optional_source_facts.claim: Probe-level timeout and termination grace settings also affect observed shutdown timing.
